newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Basis mostly unchanged.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Basis mostly unchanged.

text.p: Basis bids for hard red winter wheat were mostly unchanged and movement was mostly slow, U.S. Plains grain dealers said Thursday.
"Harvest is finishing up and we're not hearing much out of anybody in terms of (farmers) wanting to sell," a dealer in north central Oklahoma said.
Dealers in southern Kansas said the grain industry was mulling Farmland's surprise decision to deliver close to two million bushels of wheat against the KCBT July contract.
Farmland posted 1.990 million bushels of wheat for delivery Thursday into Hutchinson, Kansas.
"We're trying to figure out why Farmland did this. Our best guess is that they were trying to force a carry into the market by shattering the nearby month," a south central Kansas dealer said.
"Also, because Farmland delivered the wheat to a Farmland elevator, it means Continental's going to have to pay seven (cents per bushel) to eventually load the wheat out," the dealer said.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
